title: Ryuichi Sakamoto's birth chart
metaDescription: Ryuichi Sakamoto's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 25.9° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Seven of the ten placements whose signs are settled fall in cardinal signs, the widest weighting the unknown hour leaves certain. Cardinal signs open the seasons, and a cardinal-heavy chart is read as one that starts things.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Capricorn, but precisely: 25.9°, third decan, 20°–30°, under Mercury in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 5.0° Capricorn, Venus at 17.2° Sagittarius, Mars at 28.6° Libra. Mercury in a earth sign reads as a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; Venus in a fire sign reads as taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; Mars in a air sign reads as drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Neptune to Pluto is the closest call of the day, a sextile within 0.8°. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, Venus sextile Saturn at 2.3°, and the Sun square Mars at 2.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mercury opposes Uranus while both square Jupiter. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Mars in Libra at 28.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Libra at 14.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 3 earth, 3 fire, 3 air, 1 water by element and 7 cardinal, 2 mutable, 1 fixed by modality. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Virgo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.2° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 19.6°.
